"""
The application: the C++ one, which a Python program starts and extends with tools and commands of its own.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence

import feather_tk._feather_tk
import tlrender._tlrender
import tlrender._tlrender.ui

import djv._djv.models
import djv._djv.ui


class MainWindow(feather_tk._feather_tk.Window):
    """Main window."""
    def getMenuBar(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.MenuBar:
        """Get the menu bar."""

    def getViewport(self) -> djv._djv.ui.Viewport:
        """Get the viewport."""

    def getTimelineWidget(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.ui.TimelineWidget:
        """Get the timeline widget."""

    def getAction(self, name: str) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Action:
        """Get a menu action by the name of its command, e.g. "Color/Reset";
        null when there is none. For the capture harness: an action can do more
        than its command, such as asking first.
        """

    def getToolWidget(self, name: str) -> IToolWidget:
        """Get the active tool widget, or null if no tool is active. Get an
        open tool by name, or null when it is not open.
        """

    @property
    def presentMode(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether presentation mode is enabled."""

    @presentMode.setter
    def presentMode(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observePresentMode(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether presentation mode is enabled."""

    def setSplitters(self, splitter: float, splitter2: float) -> None:
        """Set the two splitter positions (0-1). The settings store these but
        only apply them at construction, so this moves the widgets directly --
        used by the documentation screenshot capture.
        """

    def showAboutDialog(self) -> None:
        """Show the about dialog."""

    def showSysInfoDialog(self) -> None:
        """Show the system information dialog."""

class IToolWidget(feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget):
    """Base class for tool widgets."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, app: App, mainWindow: MainWindow, name: str, icon: str, objectName: str = '', parent: feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def toolName(self) -> str:
        """Get the tool's name, the one its ToolInfo in the tools model has."""

    def setWidget(self, widget: feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget) -> None: ...

    def scrollTo(self, section: str) -> None:
        """Scroll to the named section. Tools that lay their content out in
        scrollable sections (e.g. bellows) override this; the default does
        nothing.
        """

    def openSection(self, section: str) -> None:
        """Open the named section and scroll to it."""

class ToolWidgetFactory:
    """Tool widget factory."""
    def addTool(self, name: str, func: Callable[[feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, App, MainWindow, feather_tk._feather_tk.IWidget], IToolWidget]) -> None:
        """Add the function that makes a tool's widget, by the name of the
        tool's ToolInfo in the tools model. The widget is made when the tool is
        first opened.
        """

class App(feather_tk._feather_tk.App):
    """Application."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, argv: Sequence[str], appInfoModel: djv._djv.models.AppInfoModel | None = None) -> None: ...

    def getAppInfoModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.AppInfoModel:
        """Get the application information model."""

    def getSettingsModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.SettingsModel:
        """Get the settings model."""

    def getSysLogModel(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.SysLogModel:
        """Get the system log model."""

    def getTimeUnitsModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.TimeUnitsModel:
        """Get the time units model."""

    def getFilesModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.FilesModel:
        """Get the files model."""

    def getRecentFilesModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.RecentFilesModel:
        """Get the recent files model."""

    def getColorModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.ColorModel:
        """Get the color model."""

    def getViewportModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.ViewportModel:
        """Get the viewport model."""

    def getAudioModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.AudioModel:
        """Get the audio model."""

    def getToolsModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.ToolsModel:
        """Get the tools model."""

    def getCommandsModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.CommandsModel:
        """Get the commands model."""

    def getMarkersModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.MarkersModel:
        """Get the review markers model."""

    def getAnnotationsModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.AnnotationsModel:
        """Get the review annotations model."""

    def getExportQueue(self) -> djv._djv.models.ExportQueue:
        """Get the export queue."""

    def getDrawModel(self) -> djv._djv.models.DrawModel:
        """Get the drawing state model."""

    def getToolWidgetFactory(self) -> ToolWidgetFactory:
        """Get the tool widget factory."""

    def getMainWindow(self) -> MainWindow:
        """Get the main window."""

    @property
    def observePlayer(self) -> tlrender._tlrender.IObservablePlayer:
        """Observe the timeline player."""

    def open(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path) -> None:
        """Open a file.

        The frame range, when given, is the range an image sequence is meant to
        cover, which need not be the frames on disk: a render in progress is
        watched over the range it will have when it finishes. It applies to the
        first file opened, since a directory holds sequences that each have
        their own.

        Set gatherSeq to false to open the file named rather than the sequence
        it belongs to. A path cannot say which is meant -- a frame parsed out
        of a file name looks exactly like a range of one -- so it is the caller
        that knows: a browser listing the frames one by one, or a recent file,
        is naming the file.

        Open several files as one change. Opening them one at a time would make
        each of them the current file on the way to the last, and the current
        file is what gets read.
        """

    def openDialog(self) -> None:
        """Open a file dialog."""

    def closeFile(self, index: int = -1) -> None:
        """Close a file: the one given, or the current one.

        The last file takes the review with it. A review is about its files, so
        one with none left has nothing to be about, and its notes and drawings
        would otherwise sit in the document pointing at frames that are no
        longer there. Unsaved feedback is asked about first, the same as
        closing the review from the menu; the file itself stays in the recent
        list either way.
        """

    def closeAllFiles(self) -> None:
        """Close every file, which is to say close the review."""

    def reload(self) -> None:
        """Reload the active files."""
